decisions.reason: As a small plugin close to the core shop-service offer, sunk development and fit with existing client projects still favor retention, though years of low visibility make withdrawal more thinkable than in 2019.

The ERP interface plugin supports the firm's stated move toward broader multichannel and tailored commerce support, so prior investment and strategic commitment make management inclined to continue it.

Because it is one of several similar price-comparison tracking plugins and weak visibility can no longer easily be blamed on a short launch phase, management would now be more willing to cut it despite earlier commitment.

This overlapping price-comparison tracking plugin has become harder to justify after several years and a prior related withdrawal, so resources would likely be redirected to the core business or new development.

The net price reporting plugin remains a modest extension of the firm's measurable optimization stack, and escalation of commitment still slightly favors keeping it even though its public prominence appears limited.
